Consult Summary:
- Acute continuous vertigo with ear buzzing and nausea for ~2 hours; clinician impression: suspected labyrinthitis; symptomatic medication prescribed and follow-up arranged for ear examination and vital signs.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Sudden onset dizziness with room-spinning sensation (vertigo), ear buzzing, nausea; unsteadiness when walking (unable to walk straight).
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2 hours prior to encounter while making breakfast.
  - Continuous vertigo since onset.
  - Similar, shorter episode ~1 month ago lasting approximately 5–10 minutes that resolved spontaneously.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Symptoms started suddenly during activity (making breakfast). No relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Nausea (no vomiting at time of encounter).
  - Ear buzzing/tinnitus; hearing perceived as intact (no muffling).
  - No ear pain or ear discharge.
  - No recent viral illness reported.
  - No weakness of arms or legs, no focal neurological complaints.
  - No reported fever.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting, no ear pain, no ear discharge.
  - No reported auditory loss aside from buzzing.
  - No focal limb weakness, no headache reported.
  - No recent cough/cold.

Past Medical History:
- Premature ovarian failure.
- Has taken hormone replacement therapy (HRT) — timing and current status/dose not documented.
- No other medical or surgical history volunteered.

Medications:
- Current regular medications: none reported.
- New prescription: medication name not documented; prescribed as one tablet three times daily by clinician, supply ~10 days (tablet implied oral). Route: oral (tablet); dose/name specifics not documented beyond “one tablet TID” and duration ~10 days.
- Allergies: none reported.

Social History:
- Patient provided partial address (SW four zero NG).
- At symptom onset she was making breakfast for her husband (implies household partner present at time).
- Smoking, alcohol, and recreational drug use: not discussed / not documented.
- No financial or other lifestyle factors documented.

Family History:
- No family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: none documented during this consult (visual contact limited; clinician requested in-person ear exam, BP, and gait assessment).

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results reported.
- Planned: in-person ear examination, blood pressure measurement, and gait/walking assessment at follow-up visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected labyrinthitis (clinical impression)
  - Assessment: Acute vestibular syndrome characterized by continuous vertigo, tinnitus/ear buzzing, nausea, and unsteadiness; clinician diagnosed suspected labyrinthitis.
  - Plan:
    - Symptomatic medication prescribed (medication name not documented); clinician stated dosing: one tablet three times daily for approximately 10 days; route implied oral (tablet).
    - Prescription sent to Lloyds pharmacy on record (clinician to send electronically).
    - Arrange in-person assessment by a clinician to examine ears, measure blood pressure, and evaluate gait/walking.
    - Advise patient to contact A&E urgently if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or profuse/violent vomiting develops.
    - Patient advised that medication may be taken without regard to food per clinician comment.
    - Patient instructed to contact support to book the follow-up appointment.

- Issue 2: Symptom monitoring and safety
  - Assessment: Patient is currently symptomatic and unsteady but reports no focal neurological deficits.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor symptoms until in-person review.
    - Escalate to emergency services/ED for any new neurological deficits, severe headache, or severe/intractable vomiting.

- General Plan items:
  - Provide symptomatic relief and facilitate timely in-person clinical examination and BP/gait assessment.
  - Reassess diagnosis and management after physical examination; consider further investigations if indicated (not specified in this consult).

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) not documented.
  - Full neurological examination findings not documented.
  - Specific medication name and full dosing details (dose in mg) not documented.
  - Current status/timing/dose of HRT not documented.
  - Smoking, alcohol, and substance use history not documented.
  - Hearing assessment (audiometry/Weber/Rinne) not performed/documented.
  - Any past ENT/vestibular history beyond the prior brief episode not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None substantive; minor transcription artifact: clinician utterance recorded as “charting premature hearing failure” while patient reported “premature ovarian failure” — conflict noted between clinician phrase and patient statement.
- Transcript quality:
  - Mostly intelligible; occasional incomplete phrases and brief inaudible/mis-transcribed segments. Several medication and diagnostic phrases were not fully captured (medication name not recorded).
